name: Lois Frankel
bio: Lois Frankel has represented Palm Beach County in the U.S. House since 2013 and is seeking re-election in the redrawn 23rd district. She previously served 14 years in the Florida House, where she became Democratic Minority Leader, and was Mayor of West Palm Beach from 2003 to 2011. Born in New York City, she moved to West Palm Beach in 1974 and is a Georgetown-trained lawyer.

platform.point: Lists bringing down everyday costs for Floridians as a top priority.
Pledges to protect Social Security and Medicare benefits.
Makes defending democratic institutions a core campaign theme.
Supports abortion access and opposed Florida's six-week ban.
Backs universal background checks and limits on high-capacity magazines.
Defends funding for PEPFAR and other global health programs.

economy.evidence: Supports raising income taxes on high earners and backed the 2021 American Rescue Plan.

welfare.evidence: Voted against keeping welfare work requirements and pledges to protect Social Security and Medicare.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: supports reproductive rights; LGBTQ: voted for the Respect for Marriage Act; guns: backs background checks and magazine limits.

security.evidence: Record is mixed: voted for cybersecurity data sharing with government while sponsoring limits on presidential power.

immigration.evidence: Supports a path to legal status for DREAMers and opposes requiring immigrants to leave the country to apply.

foreign.evidence: Defends foreign aid including PEPFAR and lists support for Israel as a campaign issue.

energy.evidence: Voted to ban offshore oil drilling in the Gulf of Mexico and to support rural renewable energy.

tech.evidence: Sponsored legislation to restore net neutrality rules.

education.evidence: Opposes private and religious school voucher programs and calls for more resources for public schools.

faith.evidence: Emphasises separation of church and state and opposes a religious registry.

notes: Currently represents FL-22 and is running in the redrawn FL-23 under the 2026 map.

name: Deborah Adeimy
bio: Deborah Adeimy is a certified financial planner with more than 25 years in financial services, including roles at JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Merrill Lynch and Citi Global Markets. She describes herself as a fifth-generation West Palm Beach resident. She was a Republican candidate for Florida's 22nd district in 2022 and 2024.

platform.point: Favors lower taxes and a greater reliance on tariff revenue, and blames government spending for inflation.
Supports legal, controlled immigration and opposes open-border policies.
Pledges to protect waterways from Lake Okeechobee to the Atlantic and modernize drainage systems.
Wants the U.S. to lead in space and defense against competitors such as Russia and China.
Supports pharmaceutical research and seeks lower costs through cooperation between insurers and drugmakers.

economy.evidence: Calls for lower taxes and opposes recent income, capital gains and corporate tax increases.

liberty.evidence: LGBTQ: lists LGBTQ+ respect among her issues; guns: her homepage lists Second Amendment support.

immigration.evidence: Supports controlled legal immigration and opposes open borders, citing strain on public services.

foreign.evidence: Backs a strong military, support for Israel and competing with Russia and China.

notes: Liberty score rests on brief one-line statements on the campaign site; abortion is not addressed.

name: Oliver Gilbert
bio: Oliver Gilbert has served on the Miami-Dade County Commission since 2020 and was Mayor of Miami Gardens from 2012 to 2020. An attorney, he earlier worked as a legislative aide and prosecutor. He was raised in Miami Gardens and holds degrees from Florida A&M University and the University of Miami School of Law.

platform.point: Supports universal health coverage, treating care as a right.
Proposes eliminating income taxes for working families and shifting IRS focus to wealthy taxpayers.
Backs universal child care and pre-K, funded by redirecting deportation spending.
Calls for ending funding for current deportation policies and ICE raids.
Proposes a HOME Act to lower monthly housing costs and help families build wealth.
Proposes a BUILD Business Act with startup grants, low-interest loans and lighter regulation.

economy.evidence: Proposes tax relief for working families with more IRS scrutiny of the wealthy and supports stronger worker protections.

welfare.evidence: Supports universal health care and universal child care and pre-K.

immigration.evidence: Calls for ending funding for current deportation policies and stopping ICE raids.

notes: Welfare raised from 75 to 85 because his issues page backs universal health care and universal child care. His campaign handles use the suffix III; check whether it appears on the ballot.

name: Mayonna Te Brown
bio: Te Brown is a real estate developer and small-business owner originally from Chicago. She previously ran for Congress in Illinois's 11th district. She describes herself as a conservative running on housing, immigration and traditional values.

platform.point: Wants to shift federal rental aid toward helping low-income families buy a first home.
Supports school choice across public, charter, private and home schooling.
Backs border enforcement and an earned citizenship path for qualifying TPS holders.
Wants H-1B reform to protect American workers' wages, and has called for ending the program.
Promises faster VA care, mental health support and accountability.
Pledges to protect religious liberty, parental rights and the Second Amendment.

immigration.evidence: Homepage calls for mass deportations, no amnesty and ending H-1B visas, though her issues page allows an earned path for some TPS holders.

education.evidence: Supports school choice and parental rights across public, charter, private and home schooling.

faith.evidence: Emphasises protecting religious liberty and traditional values.

notes: Her homepage and issues page differ on immigration (mass deportation with no amnesty versus an earned citizenship path for some TPS holders).

name: Jared Moskowitz
bio: Jared Moskowitz has served in the U.S. House since 2023 and is running in the redrawn 25th district. He previously served on the Parkland City Commission, in the Florida House from 2012 to 2019, and as director of the Florida Division of Emergency Management from 2019 to 2021. A Coral Springs native, he holds a law degree from Nova Southeastern University.

platform.point: Aims to lower property insurance premiums, drug prices and everyday costs for South Florida families.
Pledges to oppose cuts or privatization of Social Security and Medicare.
Promises to hold officials of both parties accountable for corruption.
Lists gun violence prevention as a priority, building on the 2018 Parkland school safety law he co-sponsored.
Supports military aid to Israel and has condemned campus antisemitism.

welfare.evidence: Pledges to protect Social Security and Medicare from cuts and privatization.

liberty.evidence: Guns: voted for new gun rules after Parkland; abortion: opposed a 24-hour waiting period; LGBTQ: supports same-sex marriage.

immigration.evidence: Voted for the 2025 Laken Riley Act requiring detention of certain migrants charged with crimes.

foreign.evidence: Voted for the 2023 $14.3 billion Israel aid package and is a vocal supporter of Israel.

notes: Currently represents FL-23 and is running in the redrawn FL-25 under the 2026 map.

name: Scott Singer
bio: Scott Singer was Mayor of Boca Raton from 2018 to 2026, serving three terms. Born in Miami Beach, he has lived in the district for about 40 years. He is a graduate of Harvard University and Georgetown Law.

platform.point: Pledges not to raise taxes, citing seven votes to lower Boca Raton's tax rate.
Calls for secure borders and a strong national defense.
Supports congressional term limits and a ban on stock trading by members of Congress.
Emphasises support for law enforcement and the rule of law.
Backs free-market policies and cryptocurrency innovation.
Supports close security ties with Israel and opposes antisemitism.

economy.evidence: Pledges not to raise taxes and backs free-market capitalism.

security.evidence: Campaigns on supporting law enforcement and the rule of law.

immigration.evidence: Calls for secure borders as a campaign priority.

foreign.evidence: Supports strong national defense and deeper security ties with allies such as Israel.

notes: Photo is a City of Boca Raton portrait tagged PD-FLGov on Commons, which cites Florida's public records statute.

name: Peter Jassenoff
bio: Peter Jassenoff is the Libertarian Party candidate for Florida's 25th congressional district. No further public biographical information was found.
notes: No campaign website, statements or coverage were found; only the state candidate listing.

name: Mario Díaz-Balart
bio: Mario Díaz-Balart has served in the U.S. House since 2003, representing FL-26 since 2023. He previously served in the Florida House and the Florida Senate between 1988 and 2002, and long chaired the Congressional Hispanic Conference. Born in Fort Lauderdale to Cuban parents, he studied political science at the University of South Florida.

platform.point: Signed the no-new-taxes pledge and voted for the 2017 tax cuts.
Supports keeping the embargo on Cuba and opposes normalization with its government.
Co-sponsors the DIGNIDAD Act offering legal status to some undocumented immigrants alongside border security.
Backs close ties with Israel and sanctions to stop Iran obtaining nuclear weapons.
Supports anti-abortion legislation and opposes federal funding for abortion.

economy.evidence: Voted for the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act and signed the no-new-taxes pledge.

welfare.evidence: Voted to repeal the Affordable Care Act and opposed expanding SCHIP eligibility.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: rated 100% by NRLC; guns: opposes gun control; drugs: opposes legalization; LGBTQ: mixed record.

security.evidence: Voted to extend Patriot Act roving wiretaps and for warrantless electronic surveillance.

immigration.evidence: Co-sponsors the DIGNIDAD legal-status bill while also supporting border wall construction.

foreign.evidence: Backs strong ties with Israel, sanctions on Iran and co-chairs the Taiwan Caucus.

energy.evidence: Supports expanded offshore drilling and opposes EPA greenhouse gas regulation; rated 0% by LCV.

education.evidence: Supports school vouchers and state flexibility from federal education mandates.

faith.evidence: Rated 100% by the Christian Coalition and supports keeping God in the Pledge of Allegiance.

name: Nicole Locklin
bio: Nicole Locklin is a lawyer and the Democratic nominee for Florida's 26th congressional district. She is running on anti-corruption, affordability and workers' rights themes.

platform.point: Wants corporations and billionaires to pay more in taxes and to crack down on price gouging.
Supports higher wages, paid family and medical leave, and union protections.
Backs a path to universal health care, lower drug prices and ending medical debt.
Supports restoring nationwide abortion rights and protecting contraception.
Supports universal background checks and safe-storage rules.
Opposes unauthorized wars and wants transparency on weapons transfers.

economy.evidence: Calls for billionaires and corporations to pay more and for action on price gouging.

welfare.evidence: Supports a path to universal health care and paid family leave.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: supports restoring nationwide abortion rights; guns: backs universal background checks and safe storage.

foreign.evidence: Prioritises diplomacy, opposes unauthorized wars and opposes unconditional support for governments that violate human rights.

notes: Security score (35) removed because no supporting statement was found on her site. Little public biographical detail beyond her profession was found.

name: Deborah Ann Meidinger Hosey
bio: Deborah Ann Meidinger Hosey is an independent candidate for Florida's 26th congressional district. No further public biographical information was found.
notes: No campaign website, statements or coverage were found; only the state candidate listing.

name: María Elvira Salazar
bio: María Elvira Salazar has represented FL-27 in the U.S. House since 2021 and serves as a Republican assistant whip. Before Congress she spent decades as a broadcast journalist with Telemundo, Univision, CNN Español and Mega TV. She was born in Miami's Little Havana to Cuban exile parents.

platform.point: Supports lower taxes, small-business growth and workforce development.
Seeks federal funds for flood mitigation, stormwater systems, roads, bridges and port expansion.
Champions Everglades restoration, coral reef recovery and coastal resilience.
Sponsors the DIGNIDAD Act giving work authorization and legal status to many undocumented immigrants.
Opposes concessions to the Cuban and Venezuelan governments and backs sanctions.
Supports congressional term limits.

economy.evidence: Voted against the 2021 American Rescue Plan and campaigns on tax reduction.

welfare.evidence: Opposed the $1.9 trillion 2021 relief bill while backing funding for hospital and mental health services.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: A+ from SBA Pro-Life America; LGBTQ: voted against the Equality Act; guns: supported background checks.

immigration.evidence: Sponsors the DIGNIDAD Act offering legal status to up to 12 million undocumented immigrants alongside border security.

foreign.evidence: Takes a hard line on Cuba and Venezuela and supports Israel.

energy.evidence: Publicly supported a carbon tax proposal and joined the Climate Solutions Caucus.

name: Eliott Rodriguez
bio: Eliott Rodriguez is a journalist who spent about 25 years as an anchor at CBS Miami before his final broadcast in December 2025. Born in New York City to Cuban immigrant parents, he moved to Miami at age 12.

platform.point: Wants to expand housing supply and stabilize insurance so local families can afford South Florida.
Focuses on grocery, insurance and borrowing costs that outpace wage growth.
Calls for restoring Affordable Care Act insurance subsidies.
Pledges to defend Social Security and Medicare.
Opposes harsh treatment of immigrants and wants congressional oversight of enforcement.
Lists protecting South Florida's environment as a priority.

economy.evidence: Calls for federal action on housing supply, insurance costs and affordability.

welfare.evidence: Supports restoring ACA subsidies and defending Social Security and Medicare.

immigration.evidence: Criticizes current treatment of immigrants, seeks oversight of enforcement and faults DIGNIDAD for lacking a citizenship path.

notes: Economy score rests on general affordability statements rather than specific tax or regulatory proposals.
